reached_at_run_time.path_in_words: Read by call path in the live bytes, nothing exercised. Import time: keys.py, gate.py, poller.py, outbox.py, checkpoint.py and graph_client.py hold no registry read at module level (keys.py line 122 is a name constant only), so importing opens nothing. Handler: poller.lambda_handler (poller.py line 479) calls gc.auth_state() (line 487, a secret-presence read, no registry) and then gc.LiveTransport(...) (line 489). LiveTransport.__init__ (graph_client.py lines 223-244) raises LiveCallRefused on every path: line 226 when IRPT_LIVE_MAILBOX_READ is not the consent sentence (that variable is not among the function's environment variable names), line 230 when the call site passes no word, line 235 when no app secret exists, and unconditionally at line 240 ('NOT IMPLEMENTED'). The handler catches it and returns at poller.py line 492 before run_scan (line 503) is called. Every registry read above sits below run_scan (run_scan -> _process_message -> gate.bind_firm / keys.quarantine_key / outbox.record -> keys). So no scheduled poll or request reaches a registry read; the reads are reachable only from an offline battery that calls run_scan directly, and from a future code change that makes LiveTransport construct.

under_the_canon.canon_note: The canon holds all six fields in infra/logic/registry/scopes.json. data/firm_registry.json in the tree is itself one of the canon's GENERATED views (lib/opal_naming.py VIEWS line 98, rows built by _firm_registry_rows line 982), so the file the Lambdas open is the canon's output, not a second source. The poller never calls opal_naming at run time; it reads the generated view file. Compared by parsing: the live package's firm_registry.json equals the tree view data/firm_registry.json in firms, pseudo and _meta (same 5 + 1 entries, every field equal); the bytes differ (5229 live vs 5326 tree) because the tree view carries a top-level _generated key the live copy lacks. The role of the aua_source, bucket, delivery_cadence, fee_scope, model_source, scopes, series_start and display_name fields is unread by the poller's live code.
under_the_canon.how_the_other_functions_get_firms: The tree's other investor-reporting functions (irpt-holdings, irpt-narrative, irpt-status, irpt-export-render and the others) package the same _keys/keys.py plus a firm_registry.json whose staged_from source is data/firm_registry.json in lambda-source-map.json, and their terraform sets IRPT_FIRM_REGISTRY to that packaged file (/var/task/firm_registry.json; /opt/python/firm_registry.json for export), so load_firm_ids opens the generated view file; the poller's source-map entry alone declares the file with no staged_from.

a_release_that_drops_the_file.reason: The live code never reaches a registry read from the handler (reached_at_run_time false, poller.py 479-502 returning before run_scan, graph_client.py line 240 raising unconditionally), and the six live .py members are byte-equal to the tree's poller.py, graph_client.py, checkpoint.py, outbox.py, _gate/gate.py and _keys/keys.py, so a release from the tree carries the same handler and the same refusal. Absence would otherwise raise: with IRPT_FIRM_REGISTRY set, keys.py line 137 returns the path unchecked and line 293 open() raises FileNotFoundError; without it keys.py line 155 raises KeyComponentRefused REGISTRY_UNREADABLE; neither path falls back. Inferred, not measured, because nothing was exercised and the verdict holds only while LiveTransport stays unconstructible; any change that makes it construct turns the same drop into an outage on the first message.
